title: Why Does Your Dog Tilt Its Head? 🐶
description:
Why do dogs tilt their heads when you talk? Scientists found genius dogs tilt about 20 times more when they hear a toy's name, and a dog's snout may block its view of your mouth.

topic: Why do dogs tilt their heads when you talk?
script: Why does your dog tilt its head? Genius dogs do it twenty times more. In Budapest, scientists tested some genius border collies that know the names of over ten toys. When their owner said a toy's name, those genius dogs tilted their heads forty-three percent of the time. Regular dogs? Just two percent. So the tilt might be a dog matching your word to a picture in its head. But there's another idea. A dog's snout blocks part of your face, especially your mouth. Tilting gives it a clearer view. In one survey, seventy-one percent of long-snouted dogs often tilted, but only fifty-two percent of flat-faced dogs did. And here's the fun part: each dog usually tilts to the same side, every time. So which way does your dog tilt, left or right?
key_facts: Eotvos Lorand University (Budapest) study in Animal Cognition: 'gifted word learner' border collies tilted their heads 43% of the time when owners named toys, typical dogs 2%
Gifted dogs knew the names of at least 10 toys
Dogs usually tilt to the same side regardless of where the owner stands
Stanley Coren survey (582 owners): 71% of larger-muzzled dogs often tilted vs 52% of flat-faced dogs; muzzle may block the view of a speaker's mouth
